title: NanoFlow Pricing Loom: Token-ledger Visualizer & Export Patterns
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design an interactive ‘NanoFlow Pricing Loom’ — a token-ledger visualizer that surfaces per-token charge attribution, role-aware filters, and first-class CSV/JSON export patterns. The goal is to give engineers and finance leads a compact, queryable panel for drilling from route/session-level totals down to the exact token spans, attribution reasons (cache hit, kv-prefix, model variant), and applied pricing tier. Deliverables: high-fidelity prototype, export schema, acceptance criteria for product and engineering handoff.
goals: Enable 3 levels of drill (Route → Session → Token span)
Deliver export formats that map to accounting systems (CSV with line-item keys, JSON with trace ids)
Provide pricing-band previews and simulated bill impact for quantization/batching toggles
success_metrics: Reduce finance triage queries about token charges by 60% in pilot customers
Prototype usability score ≥ 4.2 (out of 5) in 5 user interviews
Export schema accepted by Integrations team with ≤ 2 iteration rounds
user_stories: As an SRE I want to filter token charges to show only cache-miss tokens so I can validate cache effectiveness
As a billing analyst I want CSV exports keyed by invoice-line so I can ingest token-level charges into downstream accounting systems
As a PM I want to preview the bill impact of enabling model quantization for a selected route to estimate savings
top_level_flow: Landing (Route list) → Select route → Session carousel → Token ledger rows with expandable token spans and pricing annotations
export_spec_summary: Primary CSV export: columns [invoice_key, route_id, session_id, token_index_start, token_index_end, token_text_digest, attribution_reason, unit_price_cents, currency, applied_discount_id, model_variant, timestamp]; JSON export contains same fields with optional trace_id, request_payload_snippet. Exports include checksum and schema_version metadata.
tradeoffs: Surface more token context increases memory and latency for on-demand previews (we cap preview to first 100 tokens)
Including full token text in exports raises PII considerations — default is token digest unless opt-in is enabled by customer
Real-time cost recalculation for simulated toggles is approximate to keep UI responsive; batch recalculation runs on demand via backend job
decisions: Default export will use token_text_digest instead of raw token text for privacy
Preview drill will limit to 100 tokens to preserve responsiveness; users can request full export asynchronously
Pricing bands shown are simulated locally using cached per-token unit prices; final bill uses backend canonical pricing pipeline
acceptance_criteria: Clickable prototype demonstrates 3-level drill and column-level sorting
CSV and JSON export files validate against provided schema.json and include schema_version and checksum
Design handoff includes annotated component specs, accessibility notes, and responsive behavior for narrow console widths
design_notes: Introduce a compact token row pattern with micro-links for 'show context' and 'map to invoice line'
Use color tokens for attribution_reason (cache-hit: green, cache-miss: amber, fallback-model: purple) with accessible contrast
Provide a pricing-band pill that opens a transient overlay explaining how unit_price was derived
engineering_handoff_items: Export job: async export endpoint that returns signed S3 URL
Field mapping doc for charge-accounting and invoice_key generation
next_steps: Finish hi-fi prototype and record 5 moderated usability sessions (owners: Design)
Sync with Integrations to confirm CSV column ordering (owners: PM + Analytics)
Create backend contract tickets for token-ledger and export endpoints (owners: Eng)
